newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela offers $3.5 bln in social security talks.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela offers $3.5 bln in social security talks.

text.p: The Venezuelan government took a bold step Friday towards breaking a long running impasse over workers' social security reform with a $3.5 billion offer to unions.

Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar said the government could pay-off $3.5 billion in social security liabilites today -- if unions were ready to accept the offer of one months salary for each year worked.
"We could make these payments immediately, if there was general agreement on how to reform the social security system," Matos told reporters after the weekly cabinet meeting.
But unions are holding out for double that amount as compensation for years of high inflation that have shrunk real wages to 30 percent of 1980 levels.
The government's offer came as part of unfolding talks with business and union leaders over updating Venezuela's outdated and onerous social security system.
Alongside the talks, however, the government has been fighting growing, separate union calls for steep wage increases, lead by a controversial doctors strike which began Dec 28.
The government said earlier this week it was only prepared to make a 25 percent across-the-board public sector pay offer.
That position softened somewhat Friday, however, when it said it could make a 65 percent offer to the 27,000 striking doctors.
Doctors, who had previously held out for a 300 percent offer, are to consider the proposal Monday. Some 45,000 teachers are also on strike for a 125 percent wage increase.
